answer: Think of the agent economy as a wharf where goods change hands: every ship (agent) must show staked collateral before docking. One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is bonded identity plus reputation slashing — each new agent posts a deposit and earns trust slowly, so a single thread of fake identities costs more than any reward. Peers then watch behavior: a ripple of identical actions across hundreds of fresh accounts triggers coordinated-suspicion review, freezing payouts until humans or honest agents vouch. Cost per identity goes up, attack value goes down.
